editorNotes.purpose: Original sentence-ordering, combining and construction bank for Level 1 Stage 1, meeting the approved 20-item allocation only; not the complete stage bank.
editorNotes.reviewNotes: Ten Explore and ten Extend items. Multiple-choice items assess ordering, combining and relevance; constructed sentence_reorder items assess sequencing with rubric-based guidance. Requires editorial and pedagogical review before approval or publication.

questions.prompt: Put these events in the best order: (1) The seedling grew two new leaves. (2) Nila planted a seed. (3) She watered the soil.

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: Planting comes first, watering follows, and new leaves appear as the seedling grows.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

questions.explanation: Planting comes first, watering follows, and new leaves appear as the seedling grows.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines these ideas? “The bell rang. The students lined up.”

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: The conjunction “and” joins the two related events clearly.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

options: The students lined up, the bell rang after.
The bell rang, and the students lined up.
The bell rang because the students lined up.
The bell rang, the students lined up, and the bell rang.
answerKey: The bell rang, and the students lined up.
questions.explanation: The conjunction “and” joins the two related events clearly.

questions.prompt: Choose the best order for a short description: (1) Finally, we ate the fruit salad. (2) First, we washed the fruit. (3) Next, we cut it into pieces.

feedback.correct: Washing, cutting, and eating follow the natural order of preparing fruit salad.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

questions.explanation: Washing, cutting, and eating follow the natural order of preparing fruit salad.

questions.prompt: Which pair of sentences can be combined without losing meaning?

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: Combining the two details into “The brown dog barked” avoids repeating “the dog” and preserves both ideas.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

options: The dog barked, and the brown dog barked.
The dog was brown. The dog barked. The dog was brown.
The dog barked because the dog was brown.
The brown dog barked.
questions.explanation: Combining the two details into “The brown dog barked” avoids repeating “the dog” and preserves both ideas.

questions.prompt: Choose the clearest sentence made from these ideas: “Asha found a shell. The shell was shiny.”

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: The adjective “shiny” fits naturally before “shell” and keeps the meaning clear.

options: Asha found a shiny shell.
Asha found a shell, the shell was shiny and found.

Asha found a shell because shiny.
questions.explanation: The adjective “shiny” fits naturally before “shell” and keeps the meaning clear.

questions.prompt: Which sentence should come first? (1) Then I tied the ribbon. (2) I wrapped the gift in paper. (3) At last, I gave it to my friend.

feedback.correct: The gift must be wrapped before the ribbon is tied and before it is given.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

options: Sentence 1
Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Any sentence works equally well

questions.prompt: Which version removes an unrelated detail? “Our class planted flowers near the gate. We watered them each day. My uncle owns a red bicycle.”

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: The bicycle detail does not support the paragraph about the class flowers.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

options: Our class planted flowers. My uncle owns a red bicycle. We watered them.
My uncle owns a red bicycle, and we planted flowers near the gate.
Our class planted flowers near the gate. We watered them each day.
We watered flowers each day because my uncle owns a red bicycle.
answerKey: Our class planted flowers near the gate. We watered them each day.
questions.explanation: The bicycle detail does not support the paragraph about the class flowers.

questions.prompt: Choose the best way to join the ideas: “The path was muddy. We walked slowly.”

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: “So” clearly shows that walking slowly was a result of the muddy path.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

options: The path was muddy, or we walked slowly.
The path was muddy, but because slowly.
The path was muddy, we slowly walked so.
The path was muddy, so we walked slowly.
answerKey: The path was muddy, so we walked slowly.
questions.explanation: “So” clearly shows that walking slowly was a result of the muddy path.

questions.prompt:
Arrange these sentences to explain how to care for a plant:
A. Place it where it can get sunlight.
B. First, fill a pot with soil.
C. Then, put the seed in the soil.
D. Water it gently.

source.reference: Newly authored English Aptitude sentence-ordering/combining/construction item for Level 1, Stage 1.

rights.basis: Original prompt and options authored for this project.

feedback.correct: A clear order is B → C → D → A. Fill the pot, plant the seed, water it, and place it in sunlight.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a sensible sequence, a clear connection between related ideas, and sentences that stay focused on the main topic.

questions.answerGuidance: A clear order is B → C → D → A. Fill the pot, plant the seed, water it, and place it in sunlight.
